sources.title: FBI IC3 · 2025 BEC data
sources.reference: 2025 IC3 Annual Report · crime-type tables, pp. 7–8
sources.scope: Business email compromise complaints and reported losses submitted to IC3; not a bank-level incident rate
sources.excerpt: The 2025 report lists 24,768 business email compromise complaints and $3,046,598,558 in reported losses. Complaint categories and losses are point-in-time reporting data; duplicates and reporting changes limit interpretation.

sources.title: FBI IC3 · 2024 BEC data
sources.reference: 2024 IC3 Annual Report · crime-type tables, pp. 9–10
sources.scope: Same BEC category; reported complaints/losses, not total cybercrime or this bank’s experience
sources.excerpt: The 2024 report lists 21,442 business email compromise complaints and $2,770,151,146 in reported losses. Comparing the published annual BEC totals gives approximately 15.5% more complaints and 10.0% higher reported losses in 2025. This is not a measured change in fraud prevalence.

sources.title: FinCEN · payment-instruction compromise
sources.scope: Dated business-email-compromise advisory; relevance to vulnerable payment and change-verification processes
sources.excerpt: The advisory discusses stronger authentication and authorization practices around vulnerable business processes, including checking suspicious emailed instructions through additional communication methods or other authorized people. This is background guidance from 2019, not a new 2026 incident alert.
